name: Southern Ocean Surf Reef ("Midds Reef"), Middleton Beach, Albany WA

confidence.reason: The built reef shows as a dark wedge on a geo-referenced Esri image of 2026-01-20 that is absent from the 2025-01-16 image of the same spot, and the outline agrees with the scale-barred Bluecoast design plan (outline overlap 81 %, orientation within 3 deg) and with the City's 165 m length (design plan 165 m, satellite 157 m, -5 %).
factors: structure clearly visible on geo-referenced satellite imagery (single date, 2026-01-20); before/after pair confirms the dark patch is the reef
lengths along the crest agree with the text value 165 m within 5 % (satellite 157 m, design 165 m); width across crest 117 m (sat) / 121 m (design) vs 'up to 110 m' (+6 % / +10 %)

edge is fuzzy: the deep (offshore) side fades into dark water, so the visible-patch outline is a lower bound for the toe; area of the objective mask 7,700 m2 vs traced 10,900 m2 vs design outer contour 13,100 m2 (area uncertainty about -30 % / +20 %)
no measured as-built survey or LiDAR/multibeam of the reef located (needs network / City or Bluecoast); design plan has a scale bar but no coordinates, so its position comes from the satellite fit
the 140 m 'distance offshore' cannot be reproduced exactly because its reference line is undefined (71 m from the dry-sand edge, about 150 m from the vegetation edge)

design_version.drawn: Default outline = Bluecoast Consulting Engineers 'Final Reef Design' (detailed design for the reef built Oct 2024 (quarry establishment) to Mar 2025 (rock placement mainly Jan-Mar 2025); design volume 34,000 m3 on 2017 bathymetry; crest -1.0 m AHD). Alternative outline = visible reef on Esri imagery of 2026-01-20 (as built, in service).
design_version.why_this_one: The City of Albany completed-project page gives the same dimensions for the built reef as the Bluecoast final design (165 m long, up to 110 m wide, crest -1.0 m AHD, 62,800 t = about 34,000 m3), and the satellite wedge has the same shape and orientation, so the final design is the built version. Per Lior's rule, no measured survey is available, so the design drawing of the built version is the default over the photo trace.

canonical.frame: metres; origin = foot of the perpendicular from the traced reef centroid onto the beach-face line (edge of bright dry sand in the 2026-01-20 image, fitted bearing 30.3 deg true); +x alongshore toward NNE (bearing 30.3 deg); +y offshore toward ESE (bearing 120.3 deg), i.e. +y is +x turned 90 deg clockwise, as in geom.py and the other shapes (x right, y down = true unmirrored plan view looking at the sea)
canonical.distance_offshore_note: centroid y = 165 m, nearest edge (shoreward apex) 71 m, both from the dry-sand beach-face line; the true swash line is about 10-15 m further seaward and the vegetation edge about 80 m further landward, so the City's '140 m from landward toe' (reference line not stated) sits between the two (about 150 m from the vegetation edge).
canonical.frame_note: shoreline bearing is local (rows 440-720 of the tile, Theil-Sen, 95 % CI 27.7-33.0 deg); the beach curves (bearing 17 deg in the northern rows 40-320, 27 deg whole-beach)

versions_info: Two outlines of the one reef. Default: the Bluecoast final-design outline (13,100 m2), because per the project rule a design drawing of the built version outranks a photo trace and no measured as-built survey is available; its size and shape come from the scale-barred plan, its position from the satellite fit. Toggle: the reef as visible on an Esri satellite image of 20 Jan 2026 (10,900 m2), the as-built check; it lies inside the design outline, and the dark patch fades offshore where the water deepens. Both agree on length (about 160 m) and crest orientation (about 280 deg true).
overlay_match: good (sat2026: follows visible dark edge within about 1.5-4 m on the landward sides, soft +-5-7 m offshore edge); good (design plan: outermost contour within about 2 m)

verification.check: 1 overlays viewed and re-rendered from shape.json
verification.evidence: Re-rendered both pixel polygons from shape.json with overlay.py render and viewed the trace overlays. Satellite outline follows the dark wedge incl. the foam patch; the objective green<30 mask lies 99 % inside it (IoU 0.69, difference = soft edge). Design outline follows the outermost contour.

verification.verdict: final design = built version; as-built image agrees
verification.evidence: City page quotes the same dimensions for the built reef as the Bluecoast final design (165 m, up to 110 m, -1.0 m AHD, 62,800 t = about 34,000 m3). Satellite wedge matches the plan in shape and orientation (free fit rotation -3 deg, IoU 0.84). Later change: 18 rocks moved March 2026 (card R11), after the image; a note only. No extension/removal known.

sat: georeferenced 0.4891 m/px (sidecar, centre px checked with pix2ll). Design: bar ticks 493.5/569.5/645.5 px = 1.52 px/m (3 %). Area recomputed three ways: px*mpp2, shapely on lat/lon polygon (13,104.3 / 10,918.7 vs 13,104.4 / 10,918.2), and shape.json. One vertex converted by hand: px (397,418) -> (-1.53, 70.76) m. geom.py selftest 334/334 PASS. make-canonical was not used (own explicit rotation, checked by hand).

length along crest 157.2 (sat, -4.7 %) / 164.6 (design, -0.2 %) vs 165 m; width across crest 116.7 / 121.2 vs 'up to 110 m'. 140 m offshore cannot be reproduced: reference undefined (71 m from dry-sand edge, about 150 m from vegetation edge). The 110 m and 140 m arrows on the design figure are not to scale with its bar (69 m and 117 m measured).
every source has url, figure, date, credit, licence, registry id (sources.md). Registry text for img-10 says volume 54,000 m3; the table reads 34,000 m3 (corrected in the registry how_used note).

Gemini's three source titles carry no URL; its 'Post-Construction Monitoring (2022)' predates the 2024-25 build, so it cannot be right. Its area 13,500 m2 is within 3 % of our design outline; its '160-190 deg' orientation is unsupported. Not used.
rubric: structure visible on geo-referenced imagery and length within 10 %. Weakened by: single date, soft offshore edge, no measured survey, design position from fit.

traced and verified by the same agent in one run (fresh-eye re-render and recomputation done, but not a different person); a second look at the east edge on another dated image would raise the certainty.
